dn4:3.14: ‘Please wait, sirs, as the brahmin Soṇadaṇḍa will also go to see the ascetic Gotama.’”
dn4:4.7: ‘I will also go to see the ascetic Gotama.’”
dn4:5.20: This too: you live in Campā, a crown property given by King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, teeming with living creatures, full of hay, wood, water, and grain, a royal park endowed to a brahmin.
dn4:6.39: And since the ascetic Gotama has arrived at Campā and is staying on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond, the ascetic Gotama is our guest;
dn4:6.40: and a guest should be honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by us.
dn4:10.2: “Suppose I was to ask the ascetic Gotama a question.
dn4:10.4: ‘Brahmin, you shouldn’t ask your question like that. This is how you should ask it.’ And the assembly might disparage me for that:
dn4:10.5: ‘Soṇadaṇḍa is foolish and incompetent. He’s not able to ask the ascetic Gotama a rational question.’
dn4:10.6: And when you’re disparaged by the assembly, your reputation diminishes.
dn4:10.7: When your reputation diminishes, your wealth also diminishes.
dn4:10.8: But my wealth relies on my reputation.
dn4:10.9: Or if the ascetic Gotama asks me a question, I might not satisfy him with my answer.
dn4:10.11: ‘Brahmin, you shouldn’t answer the question like that. This is how you should answer it.’ And the assembly might disparage me for that:
dn4:10.12: ‘Soṇadaṇḍa is foolish and incompetent. He’s not able to satisfy the ascetic Gotama’s mind with his answer.’
dn4:10.13: And when you’re disparaged by the assembly, your reputation diminishes.
dn4:10.14: When your reputation diminishes, your wealth also diminishes.
dn4:10.15: But my wealth relies on my reputation.
dn4:12.3: ‘If only the ascetic Gotama would ask me about my own tutor’s scriptural heritage of the three Vedas! Then I could definitely satisfy his mind with my answer.’ And now the ascetic Gotama is asking me about my own tutor’s scriptural heritage of the three Vedas.
dn4:14.2: and so that when he says ‘I am a brahmin’ he speaks rightly, without falling into falsehood?”
dn4:14.6: It’s when a brahmin is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation;
dn4:14.7: he recites and remembers the hymns, and has mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knows them word-by-word, and their grammar. He is well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man;
dn4:14.8: he is ethical, mature in ethical conduct;
dn4:14.9: and he’s astute and intelligent, being the first or second to hold the sacrificial ladle.
dn4:14.11: and so that when he says ‘I am a brahmin’ he speaks rightly, without falling into falsehood.”
